style.vernacular: Flat Sahelian river capital where the Chari meets the Logone: single-storey cement-rendered and sun-dried-brick (banco) houses behind high mud or block walls on dusty sand streets, flat roofs or corrugated-iron sheets, and a thin colonial/1960s core along the Chari of two-to-four storey rendered government blocks. Very hot, dust-coloured, acacia and neem trees, doum and date palms along the river; much of the 1979-80 civil-war centre was rebuilt in concrete.
style.ornament: Little applied ornament: plain sand-coloured render with painted door and gate colours, geometric metal gates and screens, hand-painted shop signs; mosques with simple concrete minarets and small domes; Sahelian mud-render textures on traditional compounds.

sources.what: hot semi-arid climate ~510 mm rain; wet season June-Sept; Chari/Logone confluence; colonial core along the Chari and newer 'African city' to north and east; National Museum, Palais du 15 janvier, Place de la Nation, Avenue Charles de Gaulle
cathedral destroyed 1980 in the civil war, rebuilt 1983-1986, restored 2013
mudbrick and mud plaster tradition of the southern Sahel
